hourly.summary: United fans are oscillating between gallows humour about the drone-spying scandal — 'it's not like it takes a lot of work to beat us' — and the usual January transfer hopium (Osimhen, Matanovic), all while the £100m managerial merry-go-round adds another lap with Pochettino. The prevailing mood is a weary 'here we go again' resignation.

daily.summary: The day began with weary resignation (5/10) as fans stuck in 'new manager, same old chaos' mode vented about the club's structural issues and Pochettino's daunting to-do list. By afternoon, the mood had swung dramatically to hopeful excitement (8/10) following Pochettino's arrival, with buzz around 'Poch-ball' urgency, defensive steel, Bruno's leadership, and January transfer plans overriding stadium debt concerns.

weekly.summary: Fan sentiment began in existential crisis (2/10) with the club in the relegation zone and ownership rage dominant, briefly lifted by Pochettino rumors (4/10) before crashing again on Carrick's sacking (2/10). His appointment brought apprehensive hope (4-5/10) that quickly faded into disillusionment (3/10), finally settling into a dark, resigned acceptance of mediocrity (5/10) laced with gallows humor. The week traces an arc from acute despair through false dawns to cynical resignation, with structural anger at the Glazers/INEOS ownership remaining the constant undercurrent.
